prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The researchers used a lab dish experiment with two-photon imaging to check how local connections in the CA1 brain area actually work.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: When the cells fired a series of signals, the chemical signals released at different spots varied wildly in strength and timing.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Microscopic checks after the experiment showed that spots connecting to different structures behaved differently even though they looked structurally similar.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: About one-quarter of the connection spots targeted other pyramidal cells but either released very little chemical signal or did not release any at all.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Treating the cells with specific chemicals that boost the readiness of signal packets turned the silent connections into working ones.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The study concludes that these brain cells are physically connected and ready to send signals, but a failure in the final preparation step stops the signals from leaving.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
